lines.en: You do not hear gloomy interrupted roars beyond the Serchio? The black-hoofed deer separates from the herd of females and rewild.
He'll be sleeping soon in the green bed, within the thick scrub, blowing from the frizzy nose the breath violent that smells of mint.
The traces he leaves have the shape, do you know? Of the leaping purple heart. He prints the fat soil in this form; and the stamped clod, which he raises with each foot, then drop.
Ben this one calls the cautious “great seal.” Hunter that you read within signs; and judgment never fails him—

Oh blessed what a head of great blood pursues at the setting of the stars, and kills him at sunrise, and sees the vast body palpitate bitten by dogs and the high antlers of the brow shake the extreme quarrel!
Gabriele D Annunzio - “Il Cervo”
I often wonder what the insides of a deer feel like.
I’ve taken notes over the years of their organic structure, and I simply wish to better understand the placement of their pieces for, in my next life, I am certain I will be one.
To maintain my health and prevent the cancer from spreading, I must be familiar with my unseen body/I must untangle the various cords and threads to know who I can suffocate and where.
I often wonder how it would feel to be a housefly.
If having more eyes would allow me to see more or if seeing more would make me wish for fewer eyes.

There are no houseflies inside of the deer inside of my bedroom inside of my house outside of the world, but there is a fly in a bubble of acid that I left there while making dinner for my latest house guest.
An old man named Andy with a crippled leg he got from his daughter.
Occasionally, he’ll make goldleaf casserole and bring it over in a 9x9 tin. He got that from his daughter too.

Andy tells me there is more to life than sating my curiosity concerning the internal and anatomical structure(s) of quadrupedal animals, but I’m more worried at this moment about the long lasting effects of goldleaf.
Andy says we are all going to die, but Andy is an idiot.
He placed 15th out of 20 students in his high school class and works as a carpenter who would not last one shoe in my days.
His friends call him Il Cervo because his legs are scrawny and frail due to his disability, and how the lower body requires constant exercise lest the muscles begin to deteriorate.
If he was truly Il Cervo, none of this would happen.
He’d find a way to persist with just 75%% of his legs or, in the worst case scenario, be gobbled up by some sort of predator.
I imagine it would be a human as they’re the lot who kills for fun.
We’re truly despicable creatures, you know.
Of course you know.
But I will never let you look inside of the deer with me.
Your hands are far too large.
You would only damage the coat.
Leaves crumple or crumble beneath my feet as I use them to crumple or crumble leaves.
I’m on my way to see a girl who sees me. But what I see right now’s the sea.
“This shouldn’t be here,”  I sing to myself, annunSiating the laSk of SEAs.
But it is, so I must accept it, making room inside of my heart for the first dame to remind me of my freshly-deceased childhood retriever.
Her name was Lasso because I had a hearing problem.
I was the runt of my litter.
Vowels never stuck to me.
: Friend! You have come!
: Aren’t you a little too close to the fire?
: The cold requires not-cold! So the red child and I set ablaze the limbs of fallen groundspring to better lock our hand’s hands on the hands of the ground-hand’s hands.
: I’m just going to say “okay” since I’m having trouble parsing that one. Okay.
: Do you want to play with us, Dad?
: Dad?
: What are you even doing over here, Ami? I had no idea where you ran off to. I was starting to worry.
: Dad?
: I just needed to get some air. But then I bumped into Miss Kaori and got roped into playing some sort of card game with her.
: Dad?
: What sort of game is it?
: Dad?
: A card game.
: Yes, but what sort of game is it?
: Dad?
: A card game.
: Dad?
: Can I play too?
: Yeah, but miss Kaori will have to explain the rules since they’re very confusing.
: The red child is a liar. The rules are not confusing at all. All you have to do is follow your heart and you will have the understanding required to play the game.
: But my heart is a stationary muscular growth inside of my chest that never goes anywhere.
: That’s not true, Dad. Your heart moves all over the place. So much so that I can’t even keep up with it sometimes.
: Dad?
: That’s right. Ami is my daughter now. Or perhaps she always has been.
: But hey, that’s just a theory. A game theory.
: And there’s no way of knowing if it was my penis that created her without taking a test that I don’t want to take because I am afraid of the truth and the impact it may have on the two of us.
: Dad?
: Yes?
: Would you like to bend your lowest arms into the position that makes sitting possible?
: Would you like to bend a fork with your mind? Or are you saying you already can?
: Confusion is occurring. Will your legs bend or not?
: Bend the legs.
: Yes, I think I will.
: So, what am I supposed to do now?
: First, you must use your eyes to study your paper rectangles. Then, you must tell a story using the words written on both of them.
: If your story is good, you will earn a gold star!
: But if your story is bad, you will earn a faceless elf.
: What can I do with a faceless elf?
: Anything you can do with a faceful elf, but it will not be able to see or taste it.
: I think I get it. But if I could see the two of you play a round first, it would be a big help.
: I guess I can pick up from where we left off then? Since it was already my turn anyway?
: The sound of those words makes my human ears feel good. Please, proceed with the telling of your story, red child!
: My first word is pendulum...My second is corset. So, my story is this:
: A long time ago, there was a girl born with deer parts.
: No one understood her or appreciated her horns. And due to the extra pieces she had inside of her, her belly would bulge and make the other kids in school uncomfortable.
: So she bought a special corset made for girls just like her. And when she wore it, she’d look normal. But she’d also crush her deer parts and her parents thought that was dangerous.
: When she came home one day, there was a pendulum in the foyer- fashioned out of smoke and felt.
: And as she stared at the pendulum, she began to feel sleepy. So sleepy that she passed out right then and there.
: A group of doctors hired by the family barged into the house and took the deer girl to the hospital. And there, they removed her deer parts altogether, replacing them with extra human ones.
: And while it didn’t make her stomach any smaller, it made her feel closer to normal than she ever had before. The end.
: Great story, red child!
: You have earned a faceless elf.
: Aww, man. Another one?
: I don’t understand. I thought that was a great story. Why does Ami get a faceless star and not a gold elf?
: Because it was too sad! Only the happiest stories will receive stars.
: Stars are good and stars are special. They make wishes come true and bad things go away. But the faceless elves are mischievous, and love bad things because they are mad about their face situation.
: But now that you have heard an example, you should be able to make a story of your own! Right, Dadfriend?
: I am not your father and you are not allowed to call me that.
: Only I can call Dad “Dad.” Anyone else who calls Dad “Dad” is going to wake up with deer parts.
: I apologize for missing the understanding! All I want is to fit there. But sometimes, I feel like I will never fit into any of the “theres” at all.
: That’s probably because you have deer parts.
: Hahah. Kaori is a deer.
: Only deer are deer!
: My first word is saline. My second word is baleen. My story is this:
: In the deepest part of the deepest ocean, there was a whale the world forgot.
: It never felt much in regard to living a solitary life. And it was so long-forgotten that even the krill would not flee from its colossal gape, so feeding was always easy.

: As the saline and shrimp were introduced to the baleen it kept locked away where its teeth would be if it had only been human and not a forgotten whale, the world felt like it was remembering something.
: That high, yet low pitched whale noise that whales make was so loud and so all-encompassing that it shook the earth to its core.
: But in the core slept a larger whale — and that whale, who had been dormant for decades, did not appreciate being woken up by someone in a similar suit.
: So it bust through the center of the earth, causing the deepest waters of the deepest ocean to sink even deeper.
: The center of the world flooded, and all of that water disappeared into nothingness as the core was now gone.
: Upon finding the smaller whale, the bigger whale had this to say.
: How dare you steal my shrimp. How dare you steal my krill. How dare you take my ocean and how dare you eat your fill.
: Forgotten as you may be and as lost as you must feel, I command you keep your role in mind and ask me before each meal.
: The smaller whale looked up at the bigger one, knowing it could be swallowed at any second. But instead, all it said was “thank you.”
: The bigger whale gazed down, curious. For it had not come into contact with anyone in centuries, let alone one of its kind.
: “Why do you thank me?” it asked, somewhat hesitantly. And so the smaller whale let out another cry.
: “This is the first time I have ever felt seen,” it smiled.
: “If acting out is the cause of this...if stealing your food and not asking permission to gorge myself on krill is all it took to receive such attention, it will have been worth it.”
: “I will betray you a thousand times over so long as it will get you to scold me.”
: Unsure of how to respond, the large whale turned away. “Be gone,” it said.
: But the smaller whale followed behind it, refusing to leave the side of the one being who had ever acknowledged it.
: When the large whale went back to sleep and restored the core to the earth, it used its tail to carve out a second one.
: And now there are two cores. But who knows? There may even be a third. Or a fourth. Or the world may be filled with whales.
: There is no way any of us could ever know, for we can only dig so far.
: That was a really great story, Dad.
: Thanks, Andy.
: Excellent job, Friend! You receive-
: A faceless elf!
: Damn it.
: Miss Kaori’s criteria for what makes a good story is a little difficult, huh?
: I’ll say. My story had a happy ending and everything.
: It takes more than a sad beginning and a happy ending to make a story storied, Dadfriend!
: What else does it take?
: It is not possible to describe. It comes down to a feeling.
: A feeling?
: Dad?
: That is not incorrect!
: When you place your armfoot on the softest object, you know right away that it is the softest object! The same should be said for wordstrings.
: Only the best string will receive the gold star and a wish. And all others get a faceless elf.
: Can you give yourself a gold star since it’s your game, Kaori?
: I can not, for I have already traded mine for Nao-chan. And surpassing the upper limit of gold stars is not something anyone has ever done before.
: What would you use your gold star on, Ami?
: I’d like to bring the moon back, I think.
: From where?
: Anywhere.
: Like the large whale?
: You think the moon is inside of the whale?
: I just think she means that it’s gone, the way both whales in my story were.
: No, it’s inside of the whale.
: Oh.
: How do you think it got in there?
: It does not matter how it got in. What matters is how it comes out.
: This whole world is full of girls with deer parts — things that exist where and when they are not supposed to.
: But does their inclusion make them any less tangible than those with only human pieces? No.
: Still, there is a constant push to remove that which does not exist, but only to a certain extent. And no one ever asks what will happen once those parts are gone.
: Putting the moon back will be rewriting history. And such a thing can not be done without consequences of equal or greater value.
: So the moon will stay inside of the whale forever?
: Everything will stay where it is forever. That’s the law of the world in which we were born, and it is a law that shan’t be broken.
: What if it is though?
: Dad?
: It won’t be.
: But what if it is?
: Dad?
: It won’t be.
: I just don’t believe there is anything in this world that can not be changed no matter what you try to do.
: Liar.
: Dad?
: I’m not a liar.
: You are.
: You have always been a liar. Just as I have always been a deer.
: But together, we make the perfect nuclear family.
: Together-
: We are Il Cervo.
“But in vain we hear the gloomy roars us among the river reeds assisi.”

“You will not swim into the Serchio to follow the plague, or Derbe; and the cold river will not furrow a suppliant furrow of your arm and your predatory laughter, proud wriggling their muscles in the cold.”
“We are helpless and full of beauty, bend down to spy on our heart where it roars, farther than the roar of the deer, the ancient desire for prey.”
“Now he leaves the herd and goes wild again. Perhaps he is of distinguished loins, and very branchy. Ei più non vessa con nascent horn the peels.”
“Already his crown is hard; and his neck grows dark and bearded, and soon it will be swollen with much crave.”
“We will hear his long ones at night muglia, we will hear his bull's voice; rise the cry of his lust we will hear in the silences of the Moon.”
Kaori’s affection has increased to [kaori_love]!
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
Now what?
